newsitem.title: USA: N.H. governor calls for cigarette tax rise.
newsitem.headline: N.H. governor calls for cigarette tax rise.

text.p: New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen said she will call for a $0.25 per pack hike in the cigarette tax to pay for statewide kindergarten.
"I think it's very clear we will include a cigarette tax in our budget," Shaheen said in an interview on New Hampshire Public Radio aired on Monday.

"I think the important thing here is that we first take a look at what it's going to cost per pupil statewide, and then we take a look at what we can do to try and encourage those school districts that don't have kindergarten to go ahead and start kindergarten," she said.
New Hampshire is the only state that does not require kindergarten and only about half of the state's communities offer it.
Shaheen also said she intends to carry on the fight to get neighboring Maine to stop taxing the spouses of Portsmouth Naval Shipyard workers who live in New Hampshire.

"Income tax on people who work at the shipyard is something that goes on in a number of states, but to go ahead and charges the spousal tax on people who don't work at the shipyard I think is very unfair and shouldn't be allowed," she said.
Maine considers the shipyard, on a island in the Piscataqua River that separates the two states, part of the state, but New Hampshire contests that notion.
